question: What reader question does this figure answer?
claim: State the single source-backed conclusion as a declarative sentence.
subject: Name what the reader follows, compares, or inspects.
immediateTakeaway: State what the first visual reading should recover.
caption: Explain the figure's result or consequence in plain prose, in the host page's language.

decomposition.meaning: Record a fact, relationship, limit, or status distinction that the composition must expose. Add only entries that apply.

compositions.model: Describe the selected label-free spatial model. Add alternatives only when they informed the decision.

selectedComposition.reason: Explain why this geometry exposes the claim with the least interpretation.

representativeTrace.entity: For pass, name the concrete entity being traced.
representativeTrace.reason: For not-applicable, replace this with the reason no trace applies.

elements.role: Name the semantic purpose this element serves in the claim.
elements.meaning: State the source-backed fact represented by this element.
elements.encoding: Describe the position, form, connector, size, color, repetition, annotation, or whitespace used.
elements.whyThisEncoding: Explain why this encoding makes the fact easier to recover.
elements.removalLoss: State the meaning or accessibility cue lost if this element is removed.

firstRead.observation: Describe what appeared first at the real display size.

labelSwap.observation: Explain why labels cannot turn this into an unrelated figure.

labelOff.observation: Describe the relation and reading order recovered without labels.

pointAndExplain.observation: Confirm every visible logical element has a specific intent entry.

ablation.observation: Record what meaning or accessibility cue each retained element preserves.

counterfactual.observation: State what geometry would change if the central fact were reversed.

arrowVerb.observation: For pass, confirm every connector class carries one relation.
arrowVerb.reason: For not-applicable, explain why the figure has no connectors.

boundary.observation: For pass, confirm every enclosure or separation is real.
boundary.reason: For not-applicable, explain why the figure has no boundaries.

trace.observation: For pass, record the entity and visible path followed.
trace.reason: For not-applicable, explain why the figure has no flow or change.

thumbnail.observation: Describe the subject, hierarchy, and direction retained when reduced.

hostReadability.observation: Record the supported display contexts inspected and whether labels, hierarchy, and overflow remain usable.

grayscale.observation: Describe the non-color channels that preserve every distinction.

proseDependency.observation: State what the figure communicates without surrounding prose.

sourceTruth.observation: Confirm each visible claim against its evidence.

blindReview.reviewerLabel: Use a non-identifying label such as independent-reviewer; do not record names, emails, account ids, chat ids, or private transcript links.
blindReview.rendering: Record the repository-relative rendered artifact and display context shown without caption, prose, or ledger; never use local absolute paths, private URLs, or transcript links.
blindReview.prompt: Record the exact non-leading prompt used to request the reviewer's own explanation.
blindReview.recovered: Record the reviewer's recovered reading without forcing it into preset semantic fields.
blindReview.comparison: Compare the recovered reading with the applicable intent and explain the decision.
